chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Rafa'ah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who performs Tawaf by the House, so the time for Asr prayer enters. Should he perform Sa'i before he prays, or should he pray before he performs Sa'i? He (peace be upon him) said: No, but he should pray, then perform Sa'i.

key_terms.يَسْعَى: performs Sa'i (walking between Safa and Marwah)

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if Asr prayer time enters during Tawaf?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the hierarchy of acts when the time for an obligatory prayer coincides with a ritual act, ruling that the fixed-time prayer takes precedence over the continuation of Sa'i. This establishes the principle of *fard* (obligation) overriding *mustahabb* or ongoing ritual movements, ensuring the pilgrim does not miss the prayer window. The ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on punctuality in Salah even during the performance of other valid rituals.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Rafa’at who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the man who performs Tawaaf by the House (Kaaba), so the time for Al-Asr (Prayer) enters. Should he perform Sa’ee before he Prays, or should he Pray before he performs Sa’ee?’ Heasws said: ‘No, but he should Pray, then perform Sa’ee’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from al-ffusayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Rifa’ah who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who performs Tawaf around the House and it becomes time of al-‘Asr; if he must perform Salat (prayer) first or Sa‘iy. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he must perform Salat (prayer) first.’”
